name: @olai/web
//exports: None. This package has two products and neither is an import: a SCRIPT (`bun packages/web/src/build.ts <dist>`, run by default.nix and by `just build-client`) and the directory it writes. The one thing here that IS imported across a package boundary is src/client/testids.ts, and it is imported by path from packages/tests — a declared export list would suggest a library this is not.
//dependencies: @olai/surface for the wire, @olai/format for everything derived — the client computes nothing about the format on its own. The remark/rehype set renders notes, documents, titles (inline-only) and the agent's replies at view time, through ONE pipeline: remark-gfm for footnotes, rehype-sanitize for what may reach innerHTML, and rehype-highlight for fenced code — BUNDLED rather than fetched, which is the whole reason it is a dependency here instead of a script tag. @types/hast types the trees this package walks itself (src/client/markdown/rewrite.ts, inline.ts). @solid-primitives/scheduled throttles the re-render of an answer that is still arriving (src/client/chat/Entry.tsx). The babel presets exist only for the Bun build's Solid JSX transform (src/build.ts explains why Bun's own transform cannot be used).
//tailwind: TWO entries, and the second is not redundant. @tailwindcss/cli is the binary src/build.ts spawns. `tailwindcss` is what `@import "tailwindcss"` inside src/client/styles.css resolves — and under the isolated linker (bunfig.toml) a transitive dependency of the CLI is nested where nothing outside it can see, so the CLI fails with "Can't resolve 'tailwindcss'" until this package declares it directly. Hoisted trees (srid/drishti) never notice; this one does.
